items.titleEn: Rocket Lab stock is rising today: here's why the downtrend may resume
items.summaryEn: Buy a diversified space-defense/launch supply beneficiary like Lockheed Martin (LMT) or Northrop Grumman (NOC). If Rocket Lab’s execution slips, customers and governments shift spend toward proven primes and established programs, which can lift orders and margins across the defense space. This is the “capital reallocation” effect from Rocket Lab’s credibility gap, not the demand headline. Key Risk: Defense/space budgets stall or procurement shifts away from these primes toward cheaper alternatives, limiting order growth. Sell Rocket Lab (RKLB). The news is bullish on demand/backlog, but the stock is still in a clear downtrend (below $56 support, 50/100-day EMAs, and Supertrend) and the head-and-shoulders pattern points to continuation. The CFO’s “surge” talk doesn’t fix the core issue: Neutron is delayed to 2027 and losses are still large, so investors will keep paying for execution risk rather than backlog optics.

items.titleEn: Target and Walmart Are Winning More Shopping Trips. Bigger Baskets Can Wait.
items.summaryEn: Retail growth is becoming a battle for transaction frequency, not basket size. Target, Walmart and Sam’s Club are capturing more shopping occasions, suggesting retailers can gain market share without relying on consumers spending more per purchase. Convenience is driving sales growth but complicating profitability. Same-day delivery, pickup and digital fulfillment create more opportunities to win transactions, but smaller, more frequent orders can increase operating costs and pressure margins. The next retail advantage is profitable transaction growth. Holiday performance will depend not just on traffic and sales gains, but on whether retailers can convert additional purchases into sustainable earnings after discounts and fulfillment expenses.

items.titleEn: Why is Tesla stock gaining 12% today?
items.summaryEn: Buy Tesla (TSLA). The catalyst is FSD v15 rolling out to select customers, with JPMorgan framing it as another proof-point of Tesla’s consumer autonomy lead. Reality View + better detection and navigation should drive higher FSD engagement and retention, supporting the $99/month recurring revenue base and strengthening the robotaxi optionality. The stock’s 12% rebound also signals improving risk appetite after the broader tech sell-off. Key Risk: FSD v15 fails to translate into measurable customer upgrades/retention or faces regulatory/accident scrutiny that forces slower rollout. Sell Rivian (RIVN) and Ford (F) on relative weakness. The article highlights Tesla’s head start being raised again, while Rivian/Ford/GM are still tied to later roadmap milestones (Dec 9, 2027, 2028). If Tesla keeps pulling ahead on consumer autonomy, the market will likely re-rate competitors’ timelines downward, pressuring near-term sentiment and multiples.

items.titleEn: Gold's recovery may be short-lived as Natixis warns of drop to $3,340
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market is seeing a healthy recovery from last week’s 9% drop, with prices pushing back above $3,600 an ounce. However, one precious metals analyst is warning investors that the market could still have further to fall as higher interest rates, a stronger U.S. dollar and weakening investment demand continue to weigh on the precious metal. In a report published Friday, Bernard Dahdah, a precious metals analyst at Natixis, said that he was not surprised gold prices tested support at $3,500 an ounce. He noted that the bank had highlighted gold’s downside risks in a report published in September. Looking ahead, Dahdah said that gold could fall to $3,340 an ounce by January as the market faces growing headwinds from tighter monetary policy and slowing physical demand.

items.titleEn: Trump says he negotiated Huang's return but lawmakers slam Nvidia's decision
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. The market is already rewarding the reinstatement with a sharp rerating, and Trump’s public backing reduces near-term political friction risk. NVDA also benefits from “AI leadership” optics that can pull forward enterprise and government AI spending while Congress focuses on hearings rather than immediate penalties. Key Risk: Congress or regulators find export-control or compliance violations tied to Huang’s reinstatement, triggering fines, sales restrictions, or a forced leadership/strategy change. Buy SOXX. NVDA’s rebound is likely to spill over to the whole AI supply chain as investors treat this as a temporary governance/national-security overhang rather than a fundamental demand break. A broad AI-semi bid also hedges single-name hearing headline risk while keeping upside from continued AI capex momentum.

items.titleEn: Why is Anthropic stock lagging the broader market today?
items.summaryEn: Buy MU. It’s a direct beneficiary of the AI build and, unlike ANT, it participated strongly in Monday’s rally (up ~18.6% on the day). If investors rotate from “AI software/compute providers” into “picks-and-shovels” memory/semis, MU should keep catching bids as data-center capex expands. Key Risk: AI memory demand disappoints or pricing weakens fast enough to reverse the momentum. Sell ANT. It lagged the AI rally despite Nvidia’s surge, and the setup is still dominated by two negatives: (1) growth skepticism after “hyperbolic” 2026, and (2) a massive near-term supply overhang from lock-ups (hundreds of millions of shares into Dec/Jan, more by early Feb). Options imply ~6% daily swings, which is consistent with a stock that can drift lower while volatility stays high. Wait for the supply to clear before re-entering.

items.titleEn: Nebius and IREN stocks are rising after Jensen Huang's return: will the gains hold?
items.summaryEn: Buy NBIS. The stock is rebounding hard on Jensen Huang’s return and the “AI capital pipeline” narrative (access to funding to buy Nvidia chips). Earnings show massive revenue acceleration (571%) and improving losses, which fits a momentum + fundamentals setup. If the Nvidia/AI funding story keeps attracting capital, NBIS should keep rerating while it scales revenue. Key Risk: Forward guidance and rising depreciation don’t translate into cash flow—losses widen again and the rally fades. Buy IREN. The article ties the move to Nvidia’s central role in crypto/AI compute funding and a $500B financing push, and IREN’s AI revenue is already the driver (Q1 AI $200M vs mining $28M). With revenue up 66% and losses improving, the market is likely to keep paying for AI-led growth even if mining stays small.
